subject: QuantPath SLO follow-up: latency / concurrency / context boundaries
messages:
From: Rachel Kim <rachel.kim@redwood.com>
To: Alex Chen <alex@quantpath.ai>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>
Date: Fri, 25 Jun 2027 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: QuantPath discovery — follow-ups on SLOs, throughput, and context limits

Hi Alex — thanks again for the demo this morning. Quick recap and a few clarifying questions so we can scope a PoC that validates your perf targets. I pulled notes into the bullets below; please correct anything I got wrong.

Summary (from today's call)
- Primary use: real-time assistant for clinicians (autocomplete + structured suggestions).
- Typical request shape: free-text input with structured metadata; median input ~350 tokens, 95th ~1,100 tokens.
- Expected generation: up to 512 output tokens for detailed suggestions.
- Target SLO: p95 tail latency target ~300ms (we'll confirm acceptable range).
- Steady QPS: ~200 RPS for search/assist routes, with peak spikes to ~800 for short windows.
- Streaming UX is preferred for token-by-token display.
- Data residency: US primary but EU option later.

Clarifying questions for sizing and runbook:
1) Can you confirm the exact p95 target and whether it's for end-to-end (client perceived) or just our model infer time?
2) For streaming, do you require sub-token flush (every token) or are 200ms chunk windows acceptable?
3) What's your expected concurrency per session (concurrent open sessions vs concurrent in-flight generative requests)?
4) Any maximum allowed cold-start window or maximum request queue latency before you consider it an error?
5) Please attach a small sample of your input payloads and a CSV of today’s traffic distribution (QPS over 24h) — that helps us pick batching/kv-cache heuristics.

Next steps we propose after we get your answers:
- Redwood will produce a short SLO checklist and a recommended Dedicated capacity profile (GPU type, counts), with two options: streaming-first and batch-optimized.
- We'll sketch fallback/hedging strategies (smaller model fallback, regional routing) and an A/B canary plan.
- Run a 2–4 week PoC on dedicated hosts with production-ish traffic replay.

Attaching the simple checklist template we usually start with (redwood_slo_checklist.pdf).

Thanks — can you loop in your SRE if they want to handle traffic pattern files?

—Rachel
Rachel Kim

Subject: Re: QuantPath discovery — follow-ups on SLOs, throughput, and context limits

Thanks Rachel — appreciate the clear recap. A few answers and I attached the traffic dump/metrics CSV.

Answers:
- p95: end-to-end from client to first token visible should be <= 350ms ideally. We can tolerate up to 500ms for longer outputs (>256 tokens) but prefer <350ms for our main assist flow.
- Streaming: we want sub-200ms perceived token delivery for the front-end. If you need to chunk, 150–200ms windows are acceptable.
- Concurrency: about 200 concurrent *active* generation requests sustained, where each request can be multi-second depending on output length. Peak burst QPS hits ~800 for ~3–6 minute windows during shift changes.
- Cold start tolerance: up to 2s only for very rare scale-up events; otherwise we'd treat >500ms extra as a failure.

Attachments: quantpath_perf_metrics.csv (24h QPS sample) and sample_payloads.json — the latter includes 3 representative long inputs.

We're fine with a PoC — our security team will want a short checklist for compliance before spinning up dedicated capacity. We can share the SRE slack channel with your ops lead if helpful.

Regards,
Alex Chen
Head of Product, QuantPath
alex@quantpath.ai | +1 617-222-9801

Subject: Re: QuantPath discovery — follow-ups on SLOs, throughput, and context limits

Alex / Rachel — looping in technical ops items and an initial recommendation. Quick notes after skimming the CSV and payloads:

Observations
- Input tail (1,100 tokens) + 512 token outputs means worst-case model sequence length ~1,600 tokens — this materially increases memory/KV pressure and per-token compute.
- Sustained 200 concurrent active generative requests at that envelope is non-trivial — needs dedicated pool sizing and KV cache policy to avoid memory thrash.
- Bursts to 800 are best handled by autoscaling + pre-warmed buffer capacity or routing to a lower-cost fallback variant.

Recommendations (initial)
1) Dedicated capacity proposal: 8 x A6000-equivalent GPUs as a baseline for the 200 sustained concurrency at mixed outputs; we’ll simulate to refine. Option B: 16 smaller GPUs with cross-shard batching if you prefer horizontal scaling.
2) Streaming strategy: enable token streaming with 150ms flush windows by default. Use prefix/KV caching for repeated context fragments to cut average per-request compute.
3) Quantization: we recommend int8 for the primary model; has ~20–35% perf uplift with small quality checks. Keep an fp16 variant for high-quality fallbacks.
4) Fallback policy: automatic fallback to a smaller backbone for heavy bursts (policy-based: latency > 95th threshold OR queue length > N).
5) Canary & PoC: 5% traffic canary for 48–72 hours, then scale to 25% if tail latencies hold. PoC duration: 3 weeks of replay + 1 week live shadow testing.

Action items we need from QuantPath
- Confirm exact p95 end-to-end target (you suggested 350ms; call this final if true).
- Provide a 7‑day QPS pattern (we have 24h already; 7d helps detect weekday/shift cadence).
- Any ops constraints (max infra cost target or pref for dedicated vs hosted).

I'll draft a short Dedicated sizing slide and sample runbook (scaling, canary, hedges) and share by EOD tomorrow.

—Priyom
